seed: Double clicking a label that lives INSIDE a group opens it for typing. Separate into Layers turns a button into a group holding its own fill and its own label, so the words a person wants to change are one level down. The walk separates a settings pane, turns the white label on the blue button into real text, then works the gesture from the top level: one click picks the button, a double click picks the label inside it, and a second double click opens the label for typing. It exists because a runner once read the code and concluded the descent could never stop, which turned out to be wrong and was only ever a walk clicking three times into a field that had already opened.

steps.note: Save Changes is real text now, and it is a CHILD of the group Box 4, which also holds the blue Fill it sits on
nothing is picked and nothing is stepped into, which is where a person starts
THE FIRST TEST: a plain click on the words picks the whole button, not the words
THE SECOND TEST: one double click steps into the button and picks the label, and the canvas says which group you are standing in
THE THIRD TEST, and the one this walk exists for: with nothing left to step into, the double click means what it means everywhere else and the label opens for typing
THE FOURTH TEST: the whole label was offered for replacement, so the button says Save all rather than the new words welded onto the old ones. The row followed the words.
THE FIFTH TEST: one undo puts the button's own label back
